YOUR LANE: (a) intra-PR DRY duplication across the component/.css.ts/test triads, (b) whether test files actually cover the edge cases this PR's own commits claim to fix, (c) story interactivity fidelity. Other agents cover general styling-hierarchy conventions, React-logic correctness, swatch-group contract fidelity, and security/a11y — stay out of those.

**Part A — DRY duplication.** I already found two concrete leads; confirm both precisely yourself (don't just trust this) and then actively hunt for more of the same shape — this codebase's own rule (`.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` "Cross-file shared values") requires a shared module (precedent: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`, `theme/components/footerShared.ts`) whenever the same value/logic appears in more than one file of a step's output — a comment merely asserting two values "match" is explicitly NOT sufficient, per this repo's DRY rule.

1. `Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL` is independently declared as `const Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL = 2;` in THREE separate files with no shared import: `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/zimmProductGallery.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/zimmMediaTile.css.ts`. Grep to confirm exact line numbers, confirm there is genuinely no existing shared z-index module anywhere else in `overrides/app/theme/` this should have used instead, and write this up as a DRY finding (this is a good candidate for a shared module, e.g. exported from one of the recipe files or a new tiny shared module, the same pattern `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts` already sets).

2. In `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx`, `THUMBNAIL_REQUEST_WIDTH = 204` / `THUMBNAIL_DISPLAY_WIDTH = 102` / `THUMBNAIL_DISPLAY_HEIGHT = 136` are plain numeric constants; separately, `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`'s `thumbnail` part hardcodes `width: '6.375rem', // 102px`. Also: `index.tsx`'s `IMAGE_WIDTHS = { base: '100vw', lg: 720 }` vs `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`'s `const BODY_MAX_WIDTH = '45rem'; // 720px`. In both cases the SAME underlying design value (102px, 720px) is typed once as a JS number in the component file and again as a separate rem-string literal in the co-located recipe file, tied together only by a comment claiming they match — no shared source. Confirm these precisely (exact lines both files), and assess: is a shared source actually achievable here given the two different consumption formats (JS pixel numbers for `DynamicImage`/`htmlWidth` vs CSS-length strings for the recipe), or would deriving one from the other require an awkward conversion? Give your honest engineering judgement, not just "yes it's a violation" — but still report it as a finding per this repo's own explicit rule (a comment asserting agreement is named in the rule as NOT sufficient).

3. Actively hunt for a third instance: check whether `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO = 3/4` (numeric, exported from `zimmMediaTile.css.ts`, imported by multiple files) is also re-expressed as a separate literal anywhere — specifically `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts`'s `thumbnail` part sets `aspectRatio: '3 / 4'` as its own string literal rather than deriving from the shared numeric constant. Same question as #2: precisely confirm, and give your judgement on whether this one specifically should have been derived (e.g. via a template literal) rather than re-typed.

4. Check `zimmProductGallery/index.tsx` vs `zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx` vs `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx` for the roving-tabindex-arrow-key-navigation pattern — `handleDotBarKeyDown`/`handleThumbBarKeyDown`/`handleSwatchesKeyDown` all implement near-identical "find focused element among a NodeList of buttons, move focus left/right, wrap around" logic. `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx`'s own comment says this was "Duplicated rather than extracted into a shared hook — a small (~10-line) function, and extracting it wasn't part of this task's requested scope." Read all three implementations and confirm whether they're truly identical logic (a real DRY candidate deliberately deferred, which is a defensible call if truly out of scope) or whether they've already started to subtly diverge (which would undermine the "deliberately deferred, still consistent" framing) — check exact key names checked, wrap-around math, and how "currently focused index" is derived in each (DOM query vs `data-*` attribute).

**Part B — test coverage strategy.** Read the actual test files (don't infer from the component alone): `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/index.test.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/index.test.tsx`, `overrides/app/utils/buildDisImageSrc.test.ts`, `overrides/app/components/product-view/mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.test.ts`. For each, check whether it actually exercises the specific edge cases the PR's own code comments claim were fixed:
   - single-image "+N" button suppression (a 1-item media array should never show "+1")
   - image-error-recovery-on-new-source (MediaTile's `erroredSrc` keyed by src, not boolean — does a test actually change `item.src` after a simulated error and assert the fallback clears?)
   - media-array-shrink clamp (does a test actually re-render with a shorter `media` array after mount and assert `selectedIndex`/`activeIndex` doesn't go out of bounds — not just check the initial render?)
   Report, for each of the three claimed fixes, whether real regression coverage exists or whether it's happy-path-only (and if the fix has NO test at all, say so plainly — that's a real gap, this codebase's own testing.md requires tests for "complex state" and "pure logic that would survive a refactor invisibly if broken").

**Part C — story interactivity fidelity.** Read `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/index.stories.tsx`, `.../zimmGalleryOverlay/index.stories.tsx`, `.../zimmMediaTile/index.stories.tsx`, and `.../zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.stories.tsx`. For any story whose args/decorators expose something that LOOKS like a live, user-changeable control (e.g. a story that lets you pick a colour swatch, open/close the overlay, or navigate the gallery), check the actual state-wiring — is there a real local-state pattern backing it (a story component with its own `useState` driving the prop), or is a prop just passed statically so the control renders but can't actually do anything when interacted with? Name each story you checked and your verdict.

Report format: one block per part/item. file:line, what's wrong (or confirmed fine), CONFIRMED or PLAUSIBLE, severity (🔴/🟡/🔵), UNIFORM or ONE-OFF. End with "What I tried to falsify" and "What I could not verify". Don't pad.

content.text: Now let's move to Part C — reading all four story files.

## Part A — DRY Duplication **A1. `Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL = 2` — three independent declarations** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/zimmMediaTile.css.ts:12`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:17`, `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/zimmProductGallery.css.ts:27` — all three declare `const Z_INDEX_INTERACTIVE_CONTROL = 2;` verbatim, no shared import. Confirmed there is no existing z-index module anywhere in `overrides/app/theme/` — grepped `zIndex`/`z-index` across the whole theme folder, `zimmTokens.ts`, and `theme/index.ts`: zero hits outside these three files (only Chakra's built-in string tokens `'overlay'`/`'sticky'` are used elsewhere, an unrelated scale). `zimmMediaTile.css.ts`'s own comment (lines 9–11) even says it's "kept as a named constant here too so a future caller doesn't have to guess a z-index that clears the same layer" — an explicit acknowledgment of the cross-file intent with nothing enforcing it. This is exactly the "Cross-file shared values" case `overrideStyling.md` requires a shared module for (precedent: `zimmColourSwatchGroupShared.ts`). CONFIRMED. UNIFORM (identical name+value, 3 files). 🟡 **A2. Thumbnail/body-width constants re-typed across component and recipe** `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:55` (`IMAGE_WIDTHS = { base: '100vw', lg: 720 }`, comment "matches `bodyInner`'s own `BODY_MAX_WIDTH` exactly (720px)") vs. `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:15` (`BODY_MAX_WIDTH = '45rem'; // 720px`). Same pattern for `index.tsx:60,63,64` (`THUMBNAIL_REQUEST_WIDTH=204`/`THUMBNAIL_DISPLAY_WIDTH=102`/`THUMBNAIL_DISPLAY_HEIGHT=136`, comments claiming "matches `thumbnail`'s own 102px width") vs. `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:104` (`width: '6.375rem', // 102px`). Both pairs are tied together only by a comment asserting agreement — no shared source. Judgement: achievable. This codebase already has a working precedent for exactly this cross-file numeric sharing — `zimmMediaTile.css.ts:7` exports `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO` and `zimmMediaTile/index.tsx:6,123,128` imports it directly. Both values here divide cleanly at the standard 16px root (102/16=6.375, 720/16=45, no rounding), so a shared px constant (component imports the raw number; the co-located recipe derives `${px/16}rem`) was in reach, not blocked by a real technical wall. CONFIRMED. UNIFORM in shape (same "comment-only agreement" pattern, 2 instances in one file pair). 🟡 **A3. `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO` re-typed as a CSS string literal** `zimmMediaTile.css.ts:7` exports `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO = 3 / 4` (a JS number, consumed via Chakra's `` elsewhere). `zimmGalleryOverlay.css.ts:105` sets `aspectRatio: '3 / 4'` as its own string, with a comment (lines 96–98) arguing this "expresses it directly rather than duplicating `GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO`'s exact fraction as a second constant." I checked this claim against `node_modules/@emotion/unitless/dist/emotion-unitless.cjs.js` (the unit-suffix table Chakra's Emotion-based style engine actually consults) — `aspectRatio: 1` **is** in that list. That means `aspectRatio: GALLERY_ITEM_ASPECT_RATIO` (a bare `0.75`) would have serialized to valid, unit-free `aspect-ratio:0.75`, which the CSS spec treats as identical to `3 / 4`. The comment's implied justification for hardcoding a second literal doesn't hold up — the constant could have been reused directly with zero conversion. This is the strongest of the three DRY findings since it's evidence-backed, not judgement-only. CONFIRMED. ONE-OFF (only this one file re-expresses it as a CSS string). 🟡 **A4. Roving-tabindex arrow-key handlers — real duplication in 2 of the 3 named files, not 3** Read `handleDotBarKeyDown` (`zimmProductGallery/index.tsx:153-161`), `handleThumbBarKeyDown` (`zimmGalleryOverlay/index.tsx:173-181`), `handleSwatchesKeyDown` (`zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.tsx:133-165`) line by line. - DotBar vs ThumbBar: **byte-identical logic** — same 2-key check (ArrowLeft/ArrowRight only), same current-index derivation (`Array.from(ref.current?.querySelectorAll('button'))` + `indexOf(document.activeElement)`), same guard order, same modulo wrap (`(currentIndex + delta + length) % length`), pure focus-move only. The comment's specific claim ("Same roving-focus technique as ZimmProductGallery's dot bar") is accurate and the two have **not** diverged. - SwatchGroup is materially different, not a diverged copy of the same thing: checks 4 keys (Left/Right/Up/Down, not 2); derives current index via a `data-swatch-value` attribute lookup against the `offered` array (not a DOM-NodeList index), explicitly because it must survive duplicate display names; and drives real side effects (`setPage`, `history.push`/`window.location.href`, `onSelect`) rather than a plain `.focus()` call. This solves a harder problem (paginated, URL-synced, forceReload-aware navigation) with a structurally different mechanism — it was never the same implementation, so "divergence" isn't the right frame for it. CONFIRMED for the DotBar/ThumbBar pair (UNIFORM, deliberately deferred, genuinely still consistent — the ~10-line/out-of-scope framing in the comment is defensible). The task's 3-way "near-identical" premise does not hold for SwatchGroup — that's a false pattern-match, not a hidden third instance. 🔵 ## Part B — Test Coverage Strategy **B1. Single-image "+N" suppression** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductGallery/index.test.tsx:134-137` only positively asserts a `"Gallery"`-named button exists for 1 image; `getByRole` name-matching is exact-string, so this wouldn't catch a stray `"Gallery +1"` rendering alongside it. The real guarantee comes from `getDesktopLayoutCounts.test.ts:5-7`, which exhaustively asserts `getDesktopLayoutCounts(1)` returns `showButton: false, remainingCount: 0` — that's what actually forecloses the desktop "+1" path; the compact path's label is a direct, trivially-correct `media.length > 1` ternary (`index.tsx:185-188`). Note this is SFCC-731 **AC 9** (a designed acceptance criterion), not one of the CodeRabbit-flagged fixes (confirmed via grep across the full diff for "CodeRabbit" — only 3 hits exist, and none is this one). CONFIRMED real coverage overall, composed across two files; the component-level assertion itself isn't a true negative test but the pure-function layer is airtight. 🔵 **B2. Image-error-recovery-on-new-source (`erroredSrc` keyed by src)** — `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmMediaTile/index.test.tsx:68-84` is a real, correctly-shaped regression test: renders, fires `error`, confirms fallback, **rerenders with a new `src` at the same position**, asserts the real `` returns with the new URL. `zimmProductGallery/index.test.tsx:256-285` adds the cross-instance angle (desktop+compact each recover independently). `overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx` has **zero** mention of `error`/`fireEvent.error`/fallback anywhere in the file (full 234-line read) — unlike `zimmProductGallery`'s file, there's no comment here explaining the omission either. CONFIRMED strong coverage at the atom + ZimmProductGallery layer; a real, silent (unacknowledged) gap specific to ZimmGalleryOverlay — low risk since Overlay adds no error-handling logic of its own around MediaTile. 🔵 **B3. Media-array-shrink clamp** — `zimmProductGallery/index.test.tsx:287-318` is thorough: drives `selectedIndex` to 6 via the mocked `IntersectionObserver` callback, rerenders with a shorter array, asserts the clamp lands on the new last slide (not the old one) **and** the live region reflects the new position. `zimmGalleryOverlay/index.test.tsx` has no `rerender()` call anywhere in the file (confirmed on full read) — the identical clamp (`safeActiveIndex`, `index.tsx:114-120`, explicitly commented as mirroring "ZimmProductGallery's own selectedIndex clamp (CodeRabbit, PR #81)") is **completely untested** here. Unlike B2, this logic is re-implemented locally in the Overlay, not delegated to a shared, already-tested atom — so there's no indirect coverage either. A colour swap while the overlay is open (SFCC-708 related-colour nav) is a realistic trigger for exactly this component. CONFIRMED gap, no test at all. This is the most significant finding in Part B. 🟡 **Utility files** — `buildDisImageSrc.test.ts` (5 tests: default query, existing query, custom quality, `data:`/`blob:` passthrough, round-trip) and `mapImageGroupsToGalleryMedia.test.ts` (7 tests: mapping, `disBaseLink` preference, alt fallback, viewType filter, no-match, undefined/empty input) are pure/stateless and not implicated by the 3 named edge cases; each is solidly covered for its own logic. No findings. ## Part C — Story Interactivity Fidelity **zimmProductGallery/index.stories.tsx** - `DotKeyboardNavigation` (lines 111-121): name and docblock claim to test "keyboard/screen-reader operability," but `play()` fires `fireEvent.click` (a mouse click, not a keyboard event) and asserts `toBeInTheDocument()` — tautological, nothing removes the element on click. CONFIRMED mismatch between story intent and what it actually verifies. Real keyboard nav is separately and properly verified at the Vitest layer (`index.test.tsx:160-174`), so the behavior isn't unverified anywhere overall — just mislabeled at this layer. 🔵 - `OpenGalleryTrigger` (lines 127-142): a real `fn()` spy, call-count assertions after two distinct clicks. CONFIRMED genuinely wired. - `Default`/`FewImages`/`WithVideo`/`SingleImage`/`HiddenGalleryButton`/`ImageLoadFailure`: static args, no interactivity overclaimed. Fine. **zimmGalleryOverlay/index.stories.tsx** - `OverlayHarness` (lines 47-68): a real story-local `useState` for `isOpen` — genuine state backing, the pattern done right. - `CloseDismisses` (lines 109-119): real `waitFor`-based assertion that the dialog actually unmounts after the close click. CONFIRMED genuinely wired. - `ThumbnailNavigation` (lines 96-104): same shallow pattern as `DotKeyboardNavigation` above — click + `toBeInTheDocument()` tautology; doesn't assert anything about scrolling, active index, or the live region, despite its own docblock claiming "AC 16 — clicking a thumbnail scrolls the stack to that image," and despite the *same file* showing (in `CloseDismisses`) that it knows how to write a real `waitFor` assertion. CONFIRMED. UNIFORM with `DotKeyboardNavigation` — same shallow-assertion anti-pattern, two organisms. 🔵 - `Default`/`WithColourSwatches`/`SingleImage`: static, fine. **zimmMediaTile/index.stories.tsx** — no `play` functions at all (`Photo`, `EagerPhoto`, `Video`, `LoadFailure`, `ResponsiveWidths` are pure args). Nothing overclaims interactivity. Fine. **zimmColourSwatchGroup/index.stories.tsx** - `Paginated`/`CircleVariantPaginated` (lines 95-128, 150-174): `page` state is owned internally by the component itself (`useState`), so next/prev clicks genuinely change rendered disabled-state and radio counts. CONFIRMED genuinely wired — no wrapper state needed here. - `KeyboardNavigation` (lines 183-207): `selectedValue: 'raspberry'` is a static arg with **no** story-level state feeding `onSelect`'s result back in. Verified against `index.tsx:243` (`isSelected={v.value === selectedValue}`) and the re-focus effect at `index.tsx:123-129` (keyed to `[selectedValue]`, so it only fires when that prop actually changes) — since `selectedValue` never changes in this story, pressing arrow keys never moves visible selection **or** DOM focus. The `play()` assertions still pass (`onSelect` fires correctly as a bare spy on every keypress), but the second assertion's own comment ("ArrowLeft from Raspberry wraps to...") tacitly concedes focus never left Raspberry after the first press. A developer manually clicking through this story in the Storybook UI would press arrows and see zero visual change. CONFIRMED — the clearest instance in this PR of a control that fires its callback correctly but can't demonstrate the interaction it's named for, because the driving prop is static. Contrast with `zimmGalleryOverlay`'s `OverlayHarness`, which shows the same codebase doing this correctly elsewhere. 🟡 - `Default`/`SingleColour`/`WithUnpopulatedVariations`/`NoneSelected`/`CircleVariant`: static or asserting only static DOM shape. Fine. ## What I tried to falsify Searched the whole `theme/` tree for any pre-existing z-index/pxToRem module before calling A1/A2 "no shared source exists." Read all three roving-tabindex handlers key-by-key rather than trusting the "near-identical" framing — this changed my answer on SwatchGroup from confirm to reject. Checked `@emotion/unitless`'s actual source in `node_modules` rather than asserting the aspect-ratio derivation "should" work. Checked whether the single-image "+N" case was covered by a sibling file (`getDesktopLayoutCounts.test.ts`) before calling it a gap — it changed the verdict from 🟡 to 🔵. Traced the `KeyboardNavigation` story's effect dependency array and handler code line-by-line instead of assuming a `play()` with passing assertions means real interactivity. ## What I could not verify Did not execute any Storybook `play` function or open a real browser (out of scope) — the `DotKeyboardNavigation`/`ThumbnailNavigation` "no-op click" and `KeyboardNavigation`'s "focus never moves" conclusions are from static code tracing, not observed runtime behaviour. Confirmed `@emotion/unitless` exists in this project's own dependency tree with `aspectRatio` in its unitless map, but did not trace Chakra's exact style-serialization call chain to prove that specific table is the one consulted at render time (very likely given Chakra sits on Emotion, not independently confirmed end-to-end).
